READ THE TUPLE, NOT THE MISMATCH. The pin is (7 terrain, 1 settlement-painted).
You now produce (8 terrain, 0 settlement-painted). The count did not drift — a
CASE DISAPPEARED. The scenario the assertion is built around, the most populous
settlement painting its own south box, no longer occurs in the sample.

So this is the same species as the two vacuity guards this campaign has already
met — `the walk must produce at least two steps` and `at least one of these
reads must land strictly before a committed sighting`. Changing (7,1) to (8,0)
would make the test pass while removing the only case it exists to observe: with
zero settlement-painted boxes, the left-arrow-versus-glyph comparison has
nothing settlement-shaped left to compare.

WHY YOUR CAMPAIGN MOVED IT: four new peoples change which settlement is most
populous at that seed, and very likely where it sits relative to the sampled
cardinal boxes. That is a real consequence, not a defect.

TWO HONEST ROUTES, and I would take the first:

  1. Find a sample where a settlement still paints its own box — a different
     seed, or a different mark — and keep the (7,1) shape. The test keeps its
     meaning and you have demonstrated the behaviour still exists. This is what
     you did for `RULE_FIVE_SEED` 42 -> 28, and it was the right call there.
  2. If no sample in reach produces a settlement-painted box any more, then
     that IS the finding: your peoples changed settlement siting enough that the
     most populous one no longer paints its own south box at this scale. Say so
     in the test and in your chronicle, and pin (8,0) with that reasoning
     attached — not as a re-pin, as a recorded change in what the world does.

Do NOT pin (8,0) silently. It is the one move that makes the red go away and
leaves nothing behind explaining why the case vanished.
